outcome: Limitations in vital activity (Oswestry Disability Index, Pelvic Girdle Questionnaire, Pregnancy Mobility Index)
Spinal mobility (Ott, Schober, Thomayer, Sedin tests)
cohort: The study included 143 women with postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction who had delivered vaginally or abdominally, alongside a control group of 32 nulliparous women without pelvic floor dysfunction.
finding: The developed comprehensive physical therapy program significantly improved lumbopelvic pain, vital activity limitations, and back muscle strength over three months in women with postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction compared to independent recovery or standard protocols.
mod_finding: While the absolute effect of the physical therapy program varied based on initial parameters linked to delivery type, the proportional improvement was consistent for both abdominal and vaginal births.
